correctness.rationale: The compact simplex gives existence. A zero coordinate cannot occur at a maximum because its marginal gain is 1, strictly larger than the derivative at any positive donor. The common interior marginal derivative (1-cx)e^(-cx) strictly decreases then increases, and two coordinates on the strictly convex branch give a positive second variation along their difference. This yields the equal or one-large-coordinate classification. For n=2 the nonzero imbalance t solves c-2=2z coth(z) with z=ct/2. The right side strictly increases from 2 and exceeds c at t=1, giving the unique global equality optimum up to c=4 and two asymmetric permutations above, converging to balance as c decreases to 4. For n>=3 the tangent Hessian is strictly negative below 2n. At 2n a direction (n-1,-1,...,-1) has positive cubic variation since its cubes sum to n(n-1)(n-2); fixing a small displacement and varying c preserves the strict gain just below 2n. For the stated c=59/10 example, an independent outward-rounded integer calculation with scale 10^10 gave lower bounds 2651392808/10^10 and 389683511/10^10 on the two exponentials in the witness (degree 17) and upper bound 1399224893/10^10 on the balanced value (degree 16), giving a strictly positive objective gap of at least 164556033/(20*10^10). In load variables y_i=cx_i, at least one y_i>=c/n has vanishing reward as c grows, the others contribute at most 1/e each, and the feasible profile (1,...,1,c-n+1) meets the limiting bound. On any sequence of optimizers, each of the other n-1 rewards must reach its unique peak at y=1 in the limit. This is a theorem about imposed routing in the stated idealized model, not an ecological calibration or proof of a sharp transition for all n. The bundled verification files were inspected, not run.

originality.rationale: The bijection y_i=c x_i takes the entire feasible simplex to nonnegative loads summing to c and takes c times the crossing objective to the identical fixed-total sum of y_i e^(-y_i) in two distinct published records. The pollination record states a stronger global transition and the same high-load limit and optimizer profile. The Ricker record independently supplies a stronger classification of global ties and minimization of the critical dimension for the same fixed-total optimization. This is established equivalent coverage; the shared catalogue date does not show who had priority. Neither one particular strictly improving rational point nor naming the channels as wildlife passages supplies an original mathematical result of comparable scope.
residual_risks: Same-day chronology and historical priority are not asserted; equivalent coverage is independent of that chronology.
The two inaccessible allocation papers could contain older exact or broader coverage; the failure decision rests on the inspected exact matches, not on lack of access.
